blocks.prompt: 1 (a) Junaid covers 100 km in the first 2 hours, stops for 1 hour, and then drives 60 km in the next 2 hours. The displacement-time graph is shown in Figure 7.9. What is Junaid's average velocity?
blocks.explanation:
This is an average velocity question for a journey in three phases.
Given: the distance and time of each phase. To find: average velocity for the whole journey.
Plan: total displacement divided by total time, remembering that the stop also takes time.
steps:
Given: 100 km in 2 h, a stop of 1 h, then 60 km in 2 h, all in the same direction.
To find: Junaid's average velocity for the whole journey.
Method: \(v_{avg} = \frac{\text{total displacement}}{\text{total time}}\) (7.1.3). He never turns back, so the displacements simply add.

Corner points of the graph
\[O(0, 0),\ A(2, 100)\]
\[B(3, 100),\ C(5, 160)\]
Why: after 2 h he is 100 km from the start; during the 1-hour stop \(x\) stays 100; the last 2 h add 60 km, so \(x = 160\) at \(t = 2 + 1 + 2 = 5\).

Total displacement
\[\Delta x = 160 - 0\]
\[= 160\text{ km}\]
Why: displacement = final position minus initial position; here it is 100 + 0 + 60.

Total time
\[\Delta t = 2 + 1 + 2\]
\[= 5\text{ h}\]
Why: the clock keeps running while he rests, so the 1-hour stop is part of the time. Leaving it out would give \(160/4 = 40\) km/h, which is wrong.

Average velocity
\[v_{avg} = \dfrac{\Delta x}{\Delta t} = \dfrac{160}{5}\]
\[= 32\text{ km/h}\]
Why: definition of average velocity.

Check: slope of OC
\[\dfrac{160 - 0}{5 - 0} = 32 \;\checkmark\]
Why: the average velocity is the slope of the straight line joining the first and the last point of the displacement-time graph.

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: Figure 7.9 does not match the words of the question. Its last straight piece runs from \(t = 3\) h to \(t = 6\) h, i.e. 60 km in 3 hours, but the question says 60 km in the next 2 hours. We follow the words: the last phase ends at \(t = 5\) h with \(x = 160\) km, as in our redrawn graph. (Read from the printed figure instead, the answers would be \(160/6 \approx 26.67\) km/h in (a) and \(60/3 = 20\) km/h in (b).)

blocks.prompt: 1 (b) Junaid covers 100 km in the first 2 hours, stops for 1 hour, and then drives 60 km in the next 2 hours. The displacement-time graph is shown in Figure 7.9. What is his velocity during the last phase of the journey?
blocks.explanation:
This asks for the velocity in one phase only, the last one.
Given: the last phase is 60 km in 2 hours, from B(3, 100) to C(5, 160).
Plan: velocity = slope of the displacement-time graph on that straight piece.
steps:
Given: last phase from \(B(3, 100)\) to \(C(5, 160)\).
To find: the velocity during the last phase.
Method: on a displacement-time graph the slope \(dx/dt\) is the velocity (7.1.4). A straight piece has a constant slope, so the velocity is constant there.

Slope of BC
\[v = \dfrac{160 - 100}{5 - 3}\]
\[= \dfrac{60}{2} = 30\text{ km/h}\]
Why: slope = rise divided by run = change of displacement divided by change of time.

Check
\[30 \times 2 = 60\text{ km} \;\checkmark\]
Why: 2 hours at 30 km/h covers the 60 km of the question. For comparison, the first phase has slope \(100/2 = 50\) km/h and the stop AB has slope 0.
